News.title: Moment housesitting serial fraudster is snared by cops after stealing £35k of jewellery then replacing it with fakes
News.content:
THIS is the moment a housesitting serial fraudster was snared by cops after stealing £35,000 of jewellery before replacing it with fakes.

Ariana Rose, 40, went on a robbing spree while using the Trusted Housesitter website to gain access to wealthy homes.



On one occasion, the thief even prepared a meal and a cake for one of her victims when they returned from holiday.

They later discovered a number of belongings were missing and some had been replaced with fakes.



Rose stole Christmas ornaments a homeowner had been collecting for 27 years, jewellery worth £35,000, a Le Creuset Balti pan and a silver dish.

She further inflicted “devastating pain” on one man when she stole a CBE awarded to his grandfather for his bravery during World War Two.

Footage released by cops shows the moment Rose was detained by officers while driving a rented BMW 2 Series, wearing designer shades, jewellery and a Rolex.

The crook can be seen looking wide-eyed as officers tell her she is under arrest.



Rose was found guilty of five counts of theft from dwelling in December last year.

She was last month for five years after carrying out a string of frauds to find her champagne lifestyle.

In one of her schemes, Rose posed as a landlady to prey on desperate tenants looking to rent homes in Manchester’s Green Quarter.



She pocketed her victims’ deposits and jetted off on an all-inclusive holiday to Miami, leaving her devastated victims behind.

Rose also splurged the cash on oysters and champagne at Claridges, as well as designer shoes and a Rolex watch.

Her fraud amounted to “just shy” of £67,000, Southwark Crown Court heard.



The scam was the latest in a long line of scheming from Rose, who began her life of crime in 2008 when she stole £60,000 while working at a bank.

Three years later, she was jailed for 20 months after posing as a landlord called Sarah Adams in a £4,000 rental swindle.

Rose also left brides distraught after stealing from them on their wedding day while posing as a make-up artist.

Detective Constable Adam Stather, of Warwickshire Police, said after the case: “Rose lived a lavish lifestyle, funded by the things she stole from her victims who trusted her to look after their homes.

“These items were mostly highly sentimental and cherished.



“We hope that the victims find some comfort now that she has been caught and held accountable for her actions.”

News.title: London’s first official bathing spot is hit by toxic algae outbreak as swimmers are warned to stay away
News.content:
A ”DO NOT SWIM'” notice has been issued at London’s first official bathing spot after it has been hit by a toxic algae outbreak.

The Environment Agency has also told locals to avoid going in the water and warned it was “vitally important” to keep dogs away.



Swimmers have been urged not to take a dip in the Ham and Kingston bathing site, in Kingston upon Thames.

It opened in May, becoming the first designated bathing water on the river in London and was subject to regular water tests during the summer season until the end of September.



But the Environment Agency has issued a warning this week advising people against bathing there, due to the presence of blue-green algae, which can produce toxins that are harmful to human and animal health.

Blue-green algae, or cyanobacteria, blooms when warm temperatures, low rainfall and calmer water conditions create the ideal growing conditions for it, officials said.



They produce toxins that can kill wild animals, farm animals and pets, and can also harm people, causing skin rashes and illness if swallowed.

The Environment Agency said that during drought and prolonged dry weather, it has reported increasing numbers of algal blooms, fish deaths and deteriorating water quality.

An Environment Agency spokesperson said: “We have identified blue-green algae on the lower River Thames including the Ham and Kingston designated bathing water.

“We are working with the Royal Borough of Kingston upon Thames, who have put signage in this location to warn people that it is not safe to swim.



“An advice against bathing notice has been activated on the Swiminfo website.”

The spokesperson also warned that it was likely the section of the River Thames between Hampton and Kingston had also been affected.

“It is important that members of public do not enter the Thames along this stretch. It is also vitally important to keep dogs out of the water,” they urged.

The Environment Agency is taking water samples along the stretch of river to confirm the extent of the algal bloom.

The agency said it had informed abstractors downstream and the UK Health Security Agency had been notified.

News.title: Map reveals 44 locations in UK hit by Met Office thunderstorm warning TONIGHT after record-breaking heatwave
News.content:
DOZENS of locations are set to be hit by torrential rain and thunderstorms overnight after weeks of drought conditions.

Affected areas are likely to experience some travel disruptions and flash flooding as a result of the heavy downpours.

The Met Office has issued a yellow weather warning for thunderstorms in parts of the UK, as several regions brace for inclement conditions.



Heavy downpours are forecast across some major cities tonight between 7pm and 10am tomorrow, offering the first significant rainfall in weeks for some locations.



The rain will hit regions across Northern England, Yorkshire & Humber, the East Midlands, East Scotland, Northern Ireland and North Wales.

Major cities such as Newcastle, Durham, Sunderland and York, alongside Greater Manchester, Merseyside and the entirety of Yorkshire will be affected.

This inclement weather comes just days after the end of Britain’s fifth heatwave of the year, with the hottest day of the year recorded at 38.1C in Kew Gardens last Thursday.

Currently, nearly-three quarters of England and all of Wales are in drought conditions as a result of the prolonged dry conditions, with 45million Brits set to be affected.



As water levels continue to dwindle, 10 water companies have introduced hosepipe bans for at least 27million customers across England and Wales, with Wessex Water most recently introducing a restriction after 50 years.

Those who are at risk of flooding have been recommended to consider preparing a flood plan or creating an emergency flood kit.

Conditions are expected to ease by Friday and during the weekend, where sunshine and showers are forecast.

News.title: Bodies of missing climbers who vanished 34 YEARS ago finally found on melting glacier in Swiss Alps
News.content:
GRIM FIND Bodies of missing climbers who vanished 34 YEARS ago finally found on melting glacier in Swiss Alps

THE BODIES of two missing climbers have been found 34 years after they disappeared in the Swiss Alps.

The terrifying discovery was made by a hiker, who reported finding the two bodies on the Trift Glacier, a fast-melting mass of ice in southern Switzerland.



Following a recovery operation, the bodies were taken for identification at the Institute of Forensic Medicine at Wallis Hospital in Sion.

Wallis Police said: “A direct comparison of DNA profiles conclusively established that the individuals were two mountaineers who had been missing in the Weissmies region since 1992.”



The victims were two Belgian men aged 39 and 41 at the time of their disappearance.

Their bodies were first discovered on July 26.



On 4 September 1992, the two men planned to hike from the Weissmies hut to the top of the Weissmies, which is 13,179 ft tall.

They were hit with bad weather conditions and never reached the summit.

Rescuers launched several search operations over the next few months but they could only find a rucksack belonging to the hikers.

Wallis police, who monitor the area, have kept records of people reported missing since 1925.



Most of the reports contain people who went missing in mountainous areas and rivers.

Climate change has accelerated the melting of glaciers around the world, often releasing bodies that were trapped for decades.

Valais Cantonal Police said: “As glaciers recede, human remains of individuals who disappeared in the mountains decades ago are frequently uncovered.”

Last year, Wallis police found the bones of a Swiss mountaineer who disappeared in 1994 on a glacier in the Ober Gabelhorn mountain.

In 2017, a shrinking glacier in Switzerland unearthed the bodies of a frozen couple who went missing in 1942.



This pattern is most evident on Mount Everest in Nepal, where over 300 mountaineers have died since recording began in 1920.

Around 200 of those bodies have remained on the mountain as high-altitude recovery is extremely dangerous.

Ang Tshering Sherpa, the former president of Nepal Mountaineering Association said: “We have brought down dead bodies of some mountaineers who died in recent years,”

“but the old ones that remained buried are now coming out.”

News.title: Moment tourist hangs by rope trapped mid-way down waterfall as he desperately flails to avoid drawing in strong current
News.content:
THIS is the terrifying moment a tourist was left in mid-air hanging by a rope as a fierce waterfall gushed behind him.

Footage shows the man suspended before the waterfall as a powerful torrent crashes over him leaving him violently thrashing in the water struggling to breathe.



The incident occurred at Yangjiaotan, a waterfall area in central China, on August 15.

The man – named Tang – was the first to tackle the adventure activity and after rappelling half-way down the rope, he quickly became stuck.



He struggled desperately against the white water, spinning in circles and flailing his limbs as he dangled above dangerous rocks.

Tang revealed he was trapped for around five minutes.

Recounting the horror, he remembers choking on the water, unable to breathe.

He said: “When I was getting into the water, I realised the water flow was quite strong, but the instructor told me I could go down.”



“After I went into the water, I was immediately knocked away by the current and was submerged several times.”

He was left with multiple injuries including abrasions and soft-issue injuries across his body.

When he returned to Zhengzhou in the evening, he was struggling to walk and requested the company assist him to the hospital.



Tang was subsequently admitted to the psychological medicine department in hospital for two days and was diagnosed with an acute stress reaction.

Tang noted that the group leader previously failed to check on him during the entire journey back to the vehicle.

He said: “Only my teammates comforted me because I had multiple scratches and injuries.”

Tang was later told the company’s insurance would cover his medical costs but this did not satisfy him.

He wanted the company to compensate him for lost earnings, psychological distress and personal belongings that were swept away by the water, in addition to medical expenses covered by insurance.



The company rejected parts of Tang’s account, with manager Guo saying the guide had acted quickly after the tourist was struck by the water.

Guo said: “After he was hit by the water, our group leader quickly rescued him. The whole process took nearly three minutes.

“After he was rescued, our group leader also asked about his condition and checked his body. He had a red mark around his waist, and he said he had swallowed some water and felt dizzy and nauseous.”

Guo added that the guide continued supporting Tang while helping him cross the water.

According to the company Tang lowered his psychological compensation request from £5,470 to £2,190 but they rejected it because he provided no medical proof.



Guo said the company later offered to refund the booking fee, pay compensation equivalent to twice the booking cost and cover treatment expenses, but the two sides failed to reach an agreement.

He said: “We will not avoid the fact that this caused him a bad experience.

“Psychological trauma can be big or small. There has to be a standard. After treatment, we can use the medical diagnosis to discuss this matter.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The company said the waterfall route had since been suspended for organised groups.

Local authorities and tourism officials said the incident occurred in an undeveloped area and that they were following up on the case.

News.title: Disturbing guide on how ‘not to rape women’ in UK given to asylum seekers by Home Office after string of attacks
News.content:
ASYLUM SHAME Disturbing guide on how ‘not to rape women’ in UK given to asylum seekers by Home Office after string of attacks

ASYLUM seekers arriving in the UK are being handed booklets warning them that sex with children is illegal, and that men and women are equal under UK law.

The nine-page document, published by the Home Office, tells migrants that they understand “laws and customs here may be different from your home country”.



Under one page headed ‘Gender Equality’, arrivals are told that women can work, study, and travel freely without needing permission from a man in the UK.

Another page on domestic abuse warns that you could be arrested or go to prison if you carry out physical, or emotional attacks on their partner.



There is a section on sex and consent which warns asylum seekers “never try to have sex with someone who is asleep, drunk, or unable to consent clearly”.

It states: “In the UK, the law is clear and strict: both people must agree to sex or sexual contact of any kind.”



The pamphlet also informs asylum seekers not to have sex with children.

It reads: “The legal age of consent in the UK is 16. This means that anyone under the age of 16 is considered a child and cannot legally agree to have sex.

“Sex with someone under the age of 16 is a serious crime in the UK. There are no exceptions to this rule.



“Even if they say yes, it is still illegal. You could go to prison, lose your support and accommodation, and it will affect your asylum claim.”

Making sexual comments in public, or following people, are also something asylum seekers are told never to do.

It states: “When you are in public spaces, alone or with friends, you must never:

“• make sexual comments to someone, even if you think it is a compliment

“• whistle or make kissing noises at someone



“• follow someone or block their path

“• make rude or offensive gestures

“• verbally abuse someone because of their gender, religion, or how they look.”



The Sun understands the resources were produced for asylum seekers so there can be “no possible misunderstanding” of what is expected under UK law.

It follows several high profile cases in which migrants convicted of sexual offences in the UK claimed in court to not understand the law.

A migrant who sexually assaulted a 14-year-old schoolgirl whilst living at an asylum hotel in Epping was said to have told her that it is normal to marry children “in his country”.



Ethiopian Hadush Kebatu, was sentenced for sexual assault before being deported to Ethiopia.

The young victim, who cannot be named for legal reasons, told the court:

“He kept asking to come back with us or trying to get us to go back to the Bell Hotel with him.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

She said: “He pointed at me first and he said I want one baby from you and one from each of your friends.

“He told us as well that in his country it is normal to marry 14 year olds.”

News.title: At least 23 killed and five injured as packed bus ploughs into truck in horror head-on smash on busy highway in Brazil
News.content:
AT least 23 people have been killed in a horror smash when a bus carrying medical patients and a truck collided in Brazil.

The head-on collision occurred on a motorway when the truck veered into the other vehicle’s lane, local police said.



Footage from the crash site in Parana state in Brazil‘s south shows the mangled remains of the bus that was almost entirely smashed to pieces.

The council health department bus was transporting patients to medical centres in the city of Curitiba when it was hit at about 3.30am local time (7.30am BST).



Two children were among the dead, as was the driver of the truck.

“At least 23 deaths have been confirmed. Most of the victims were on the bus,” local authorities said.

At least five people were also injured with three of the survivors in a serious condition, officials said.

The nightmare smash occurred on a highway that connects the southern part of the country with Sao Paulo, Brazil’s wealthiest state.



State governor Ratinho Junior said: “In light of the tragedy in Ipiranga, I have declared three days of official mourning throughout the state.

“At this moment of profound grief, my solidarity is with the families who lost their loved ones and with all those who were injured.”

Eduardo Pimentel, mayor of Parana’s state capital Curitiba, said: “I received with sadness the news of the serious accident on BR-373, in Ipiranga, involving a Health Department minibus from Imbituva.

“They were patients and companions who were coming to the Curitiba region seeking medical care.

“At this moment of pain, my solidarity is with the families and friends of the victims and with the entire population of Imbituva.



“I ask God to comfort every heart and give strength to the injured in their recovery.

“Curitiba joins Parana in prayer in the face of this tragedy.”

The collision has been described as the worst road accident in Parana for more than five years, when 19 people died after a bus crashed in the city of Guaratuba in January 2021.

Fatal traffic collisions are common in Brazil, with eight people dying in the state of Rio de Janeiro on Sunday when the bus they were travelling in overturned.

In February, a bus returning from a religious festival in northeastern Brazil veered off the road and flipped, killing at least 16 people.

A SYRIAN national has been charged with sexual assault of two girls aged under 16.

Police were called to reports two girls had been sexually assaulted at a hotel in Kenilworth, Warwickshire, on Monday evening.



Officers located both girls at the hotel and later that same night, arrested a 27-year-old Syrian national at his home address.

News.title: UK's longest-serving prisoner Robert Maudsley: I want to stay behind bars – I could kill again
News.content:
UK's longest-serving prisoner Robert Maudsley: I want to stay behind bars – I could kill again

EXCLUSIVE: In his first interview in almost 50 years, quadruple killer Robert Maudsley, 73, spoke to the Mirror from his prison cell on E Wing in HMP Whitemoor, Cambridgeshire

Robert Maudsley - Corrections

Britain's longest serving prisoner has told of his 17,500 consecutive days in solitary confinement - and warns that he could kill again.

‌



In his first interview in 50 years, quadruple killer Robert Maudsley, 73, spoke to the Mirror from 'E' Wing of HMP Whitemoor, Cambridgeshire.

‌



Maudsley was nicknamed 'Hannibal the Cannibal' after he killed a fellow inmate and was said to have eaten his brain with a spoon. A post-mortem proved that claim untrue.

‌



The shocking case has been likened to the fictional killer Hannibal Lecter in the 1991 hit movie 'The Silence of the Lambs,' the disturbing portrayal of a cannibalistic serial killer for which Anthony Hopkins won an Oscar.

Maudsley has spent the best part of 47 years either in segregation or solitary, setting a world record of 17,500 consecutive days alone.

He has now served 52 years behind bars, and was once described as the most dangerous prisoner in the UK penal system.

‌



After killing three fellow inmates, he was deemed such a risk that he had to stick his feet out of a gap at the bottom of his cell door to have his toenails clipped.

In a wide-ranging, hour-long interview, he spoke about his life behind bars, how he has found love for the first time with his partner Loveinia MacKenney, and why he believes that he should be locked up for life.

He told the Mirror: "I have to be honest and say that if I had the opportunity to harm a sex offender then I would do so. If I met someone who had sexually abused me, I would do my best to kill them.

‌



"When I went back to Liverpool, I had the desire to kill both my parents, and then I had the desire to harm myself. I wanted to get my own back, including on my father, and I visualised killing my parents."

View 5 Images The last time Robert Maudsley was seen by the outside world was in a documentary almost 50 years ago (Image: BBC)

Parents' nicknames

Maudsley, one of 12 children, told his prison psychologist Dr Bob Johnson, also interviewed by the Mirror, that his father abused him and locked him in a cupboard under the stairs at the family home.

‌



Known as 'Uncle Bob' to his family, Maudsley added: "We called them the drunk, and the witch. We referred to them by those names rather than as mother and father.

"I do have the possibility within myself to kill again, but with therapy, I think that I could overcome that."

Maudsley killed two people in one day

Prison barbers refused to enter Maudsley's cell in Wakefield jail after he killed two inmates there on the same day in 1977.

‌



He told a prison guard, "You'll be two down on the roll call," after walking away from his victims' bodies.

He grew his hair and beard long, and refused to co-operate with prison staff.

A Perspex wall had to be installed in his 18 ft by 15 ft wide cell so he could not throw liquids or missiles at his guards.

‌



That again led to comparisons with the cell that held the fictitious killer Hannibal Lecter.

"On the high security unit at Wakefield, when they built them, the cell door opened flush to the wall," Maudsley recalled.

"About two feet in front of the cell door, there was a barred gate with Perspex so I could not throw anything at the guards when they entered.

‌



"It was like a normal cell except down the centre of it, there was a TV shared with the cell next door.

"It had wires connected to speakers inside our cells. We had to flip the speaker, there was a diagonal screen so we could then watch the TV.

"I was not in a Perspex box but it did have the Perspex wall. For a long time I just had a mattress and a pot to pee in.

‌



"I would have to put my feet through a gap in the door for the officers to cut my toenails.

"For 12-13 months I did not shave or cut my hair, and yes, I was like the Wild Man of Borneo."

View 5 Images Robert Maudsley as a child in his native Liverpool (Image: Liverpool Echo)

‌



Charlie Bronson

He laughs but adds: "It was psychological. I thought that if you want to treat me like an animal, I will act like one.

"I am refusing all prison food at the moment. I buy whatever I can get from the prison shop in protest at the way I am being treated.

"That is about the refusal of my visits, my conditions overall."

‌



For many years at Wakefield, the notorious prisoner Charlie Bronson was his 'next door neighbour' and they shared the TV in their high-security cells.

"They (cells) were mirror images of each other. We could talk to each other through the windows," added Maudsley.

"But we did not really get on.

‌



"He was a narcissist, he always had to be top dog, trying to put me down at every opportunity to establish dominance.

"We had a falling-out over what programme to watch one night. So I asked a prison guard to open the gap for the TV and I put my foot through it.

"Charlie was not very happy about that." Maudsley says his treatment at Whitemoor has been 'sinister'.

‌



View 5 Images Robert Maudsley seen as a young man in his prison cell. He is now 73, and has spent 52 years behind bars (Image: Unknown)

"They believed the stories in the newspapers and books," he added.

"They thought I was dangerous, then their treatment became more sinister.

‌



"They put me on the punishment yard, that is the thing that gets to me.

"You cannot see anything, the walls are so high, there is no pond, it is sterile.

"I can hear the other prisoners laughing and joking with each other.

‌



"It was the prison staff who got sick of that regime. They got bored with it."

Maudsley, Prisoner A9888AA, was first sent to Broadmoor in 1974 for the manslaughter of child sex offender John Farrell.

He killed another patient, a convicted child molester, at the high-security hospital in 1976.

‌



He was then moved to Wakefield, where he murdered two of his fellow inmates, both described as child sex offenders.

He is unapologetic about the deaths of any of his victims.

View 5 Images Loveinia MacKenney has been writing to Robert Maudsley for around five years (Image: Daily Mirror)

‌



Gogglebox

When he last tasted freedom at the age of 21 in 1974, Harold Wilson had just succeeded Edward Heath as Prime Minister, a loaf of white bread cost 14p and Paper Lace were at No 1 with 'Billy, Don't Be A Hero'.

He is fighting to see Loveinia and has not had a visit since Feb. 2025. He is desperate to meet her for the first time after almost five years of correspondence and phone calls.

‌



He claims visit requests since his transfer to Whitemoor from Wakefield in April, 2025, have been refused.

"The denial of visits has added to my isolation, there is no doubt about that," he said. "I am locked in my cell for 22 and a half hours per day, getting only 75 minutes to exercise and shower.

"I always put the radio on in the morning and listen to Magic Classical. I love classical music. I watch TV.

‌



"Now I get 28 channels. My favourite show is Gogglebox, and I like The Chase with Bradley Walsh, Pointless, and Countdown.

"I watch them, to keep my mind occupied and active so I don't start to deteriorate."

'I see the whole life term as justified'

Despite early prisoner release, he insisted: "I want to spend the rest of my life behind bars to pay for what I have done.

‌



"I see the whole life term as justified for my crimes. The way I cope is that every time I wake up in the morning I think, 'It is a new day'.

"It may be like what I have experienced before, but there may be something different."

After spending almost his entire adult life in solitary confinement, he finds joy in a wisp of a breeze coming through his cell window.

‌



He would love to experience 'winter, autumn, spring, and summer again'. "To feel the wind when it blows through my window at night is fantastic," he said. "To feel the sun on your skin, it is the little things that you miss."

The last time the outside world saw him, he was in his 20s during the filming of a BBC documentary.

He says that he now looks like the late American country singer Kenny Rogers, due to his clipped white beard and hair.

‌



He loves Schubert's "Ave Maria". "It is beautiful," he says. "When you listen to that, you are no longer in the prison cell, you could be anywhere in the world.

"Mozart also did some beautiful things. A pop record can take me back to my childhood.

"For me, it is the Rolling Stones rather than the Beatles. "

‌



Given the chance to taste freedom, he would live on an island with Londoner Loveinia, 71, a mum-of-one.

With her, he has found love for the first time in his life.

"With my parents, there was no love," he says. "It has given me hope and for as long as we are alive, we will both have each other and give each other strength. The love we share keeps us going, it is the first time I have ever loved someone in the way that I love her."

‌



View 5 Images A letter from Maudsley about his treatment

Psychiatrist Bob Johnson, 89, who treated Maudsley in Parkhurst back in the 1980s, said: "I would sit alone with him in his cell and we'd discuss our favourite composer Schubert.

"It would be far better to use his intelligence and get him working, he could have earned thousands in compensation to be paid to the victims' families.

‌



"I believe that he would not have killed again with the help of our sessions. What he has had since is institutional sadism."

In the Hollywood film 'The Shawshank Redemption,' the Morgan Freeman character Ellis 'Red' Redding is asked what he would say if he could speak to his younger self, before he committed his crimes.

Maudsley was asked the same question. He replied: "It is difficult because there are so many thanks that I could say to that 20-year-old.

Article continues below

"The main thing, irrespective of what happened, is that I had the strength to get up. I know inwardly that I would have the strength to keep going."

There is no regret for his 52 years behind bars. Unlike Red in the film, he has no desire to change: "The people I killed did not see their victims as human, in a sense I was a piece of meat.

"I treated them the same, and got my revenge that way. If I say that I should not have done that, the years in prison would be worthless."

News.title: GCSE results: 20 stars who prove you don't need good grades for success
News.content:
GCSE results: 20 stars who prove you don't need good grades for success

Jeremy Clarkson, Cheryl, Robbie Williams and Simon Cowell are among the famous faces who found success despite disappointing grades or setbacks at school.

View 21 Images Jeremy Clarkson, Cheryl and Robbie Williams all suffered setbacks at school (Image: Getty)

From Jeremy Clarkson and Cheryl to Hollywood stars and successful entrepreneurs, plenty of famous faces found huge success despite disappointing results or setbacks at school.

‌



Students across the country will find out their GCSE results on Thursday, after weeks of waiting to discover whether all those hours of revision paid off.

‌



Some of the biggest names in entertainment and business left school with few qualifications, failed exams or were rejected from the courses they desperately wanted.

‌



Others took a different route entirely before building careers worth millions or becoming household names around the world.

For older stars on the list, GCSEs had not yet been introduced and they instead sat O-levels, the qualification they later replaced.

Here are 20 famous faces whose school days did not go entirely to plan...

‌



Jeremy Clarkson

Jeremy Clarkson has regularly used results day to remind students that disappointing grades do not necessarily dictate what comes next.

On A-level results day, he wrote on X: “Don’t worry if your A level results are a bit disappointing. I got a C and two Us. And this evening I shall sit in my agreeable garden, drinking beer from my own brewery and eating food from my own farm. Prepared by my own chef.”

It certainly did not stop him building a hugely successful television career, presenting Top Gear, The Grand Tour and Clarkson's Farm.

‌



View 21 Images Jeremy Clarkson (Image: Matthew Vincent/PA Wire)

Cheryl

Cheryl left school at 16 without taking GCSEs and instead focused on trying to build a career in music. That decision paid off when she won a place in Girls Aloud on Popstars: The Rivals in 2002.

Writing in her book Through My Eyes, she said: “Ever since I was a kid I've loved performing, being on stage, singing, dancing and showing off. There was just always something inside me, like, I knew there was no other option.”

‌



She went on to enjoy huge success with Girls Aloud before launching a solo career and becoming a television judge.

View 21 Images Cheryl (Image: Getty Images)

Robbie Williams

Robbie Williams has spoken openly about leaving school without any GCSE qualifications and later feeling that his dyslexia, dyscalculia and ADHD had gone unrecognised at the time.

‌



The singer has even said he would like to return to education and resit his exams after revealing he achieved nothing higher than a D.

He previously told The Sun: “I’ve been wanting to set up a university but, actually, I wouldn’t be able to attend if and when I do, because I didn’t get any GCSEs. I got nothing higher than a grade D, and everything else I failed or I didn’t turn up for. I really want to go back and get them.”

Williams went on to achieve huge success with Take That before becoming one of Britain’s most successful solo artists.

‌



View 21 Images Robbie Williams (Image: Dave Benett/Getty Images for FLANNELS and Hopeium)

Simon Cowell

Simon Cowell left school at 16 with just one O-level. He started out working in the mailroom at EMI Music Publishing before moving into talent scouting and the record business.

Cowell eventually became one of the best-known figures in entertainment through shows including The X Factor and Britain's Got Talent.

‌



View 21 Images Simon Cowell (Image: Getty Images)

Sir Richard Branson

Sir Richard Branson left school without any qualifications before going on to build the Virgin business empire.

Rather than following an academic route, he focused on business and later launched Virgin, which grew to include more than 100 companies.

‌



Reflecting on exam results on his blog, Branson wrote: “My suggestion is to not get too caught up in grades and concentrate on goals. Some people point rightly to the likes of Albert Einstein, Steve Jobs, Sir Winston Churchill and Bill Gates and note that they all failed exams. They all went on to achieve great things.”

View 21 Images Sir Richard Branson (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

Jamie Oliver

Jamie Oliver has been open about leaving school with just two GCSEs before building a hugely successful career in food.

‌



On GCSE results day last year, the chef used Instagram to reassure students who may not have received the grades they wanted.

He wrote: “Whatever your results, you’ve done brilliantly. Even if they’re not what you expected, you’re going to be just fine. Remember, school is just one part of your journey.”

Oliver then pointed to his own experience, adding: “I came out of school with just two GCSEs, and look at me now! 30 cookbooks, done – and more to come."

‌



He went on to say he believes schools should celebrate different types of ability and help all children build confidence and thrive.

View 21 Images Jamie Oliver (Image: SWNS)

Sarah Millican

Sarah Millican has previously offered reassurance to students disappointed by their exam results by revealing her own A-level grades.

‌



The comedian said she received two D's and an E and told young people that not getting the grades they wanted was not the end of the world.

She went on to build a hugely successful stand-up career and become a regular face on British television.

View 21 Images Sarah Millican (Image: PA)

‌



Jon Snow

Jon Snow went on to become one of the UK’s best-known broadcasters, but his A-level results were far from straightforward.

He got a C in English and failed his other subjects, before later achieving a D and an E in economics and law.

Snow then went to college to improve his qualifications and eventually secured a place at the University of Liverpool to study law through clearing.

‌



His advice to students has been simple: “Want to do what you want to do very badly,” adding: “There is life after A-levels.”

View 21 Images Jon Snow (Image: PA)

James Corden

James Corden left school with just two GCSEs, but went on to build a hugely successful career in television and entertainment.

‌



He became a household name through Gavin & Stacey before later hosting The Late Late Show in the US and appearing in a string of films and stage productions.

View 21 Images James Corden (Image: Getty Images for SiriusXM)

Benedict Cumberbatch

Benedict Cumberbatch has admitted his interest in academic success dipped after an impressive set of GCSE results.

‌



The actor told the Metro he had “blown” his GCSEs “out of the water”, creating expectations that he would reach an Oxbridge standard at A-level.

But he later admitted becoming distracted as a teenager and getting “a bit lazy”. It did little to hold back his acting career, with Cumberbatch going on to become one of Britain's most recognisable film and television stars.

View 21 Images Benedict Cumberbatch (Image: Getty Images for SBIFF)

‌



Theo Paphitis

Dragons' Den star Theo Paphitis left school at 16 without qualifications after struggling with dyslexia. He started his working life as a filing clerk before moving into retail and entrepreneurship.

Paphitis went on to build a major business career involving brands including Ryman and Robert Dyas.

View 21 Images Theo Paphitis (Image: MDM)

‌



Jo Malone

Jo Malone struggled with dyslexia at school and left without qualifications. She later turned her interest in fragrance into a hugely successful business career.

She founded Jo Malone London before later launching Jo Loves.

View 21 Images Jo Malone (Image: PA)

‌



Deborah Meaden

Deborah Meaden left school before completing her A-levels and instead went on to study business at college.

She later built a successful career in business, including running a multi-million-pound family holiday company, before becoming one of the best-known investors on Dragons' Den.

View 21 Images Deborah Meaden (Image: PA)

‌



Guy Ritchie

Guy Ritchie left school at the age of 15 after struggling with education and has said his only qualification is a GCSE in film studies.

The director, who has dyslexia, recalled attending around 10 schools and said he was “appalling” at all of them. He later found his way into filmmaking, beginning as a runner before moving into commercials and music videos.

View 21 Images Guy Ritchie (Image: Variety via Getty Images)

‌



Carey Mulligan

Carey Mulligan faced a major setback when she tried to turn her interest in acting into a career. As a teenager, she was rejected by Rada, Central and Drama Centre London.

She broke into acting and went on to establish herself as one of Britain's most acclaimed film stars.

View 21 Images Carey Mulligan (Image: Variety via Getty Images)

‌



Alan Sugar

Lord Alan Sugar has previously used GCSE results day to reassure students who did not get the grades they hoped for.

Writing on X in 2017, he said: “GCSE RESULTS. If you didn't get the grades don't panic. @richardbranson didn't get any I never went to UNI. Get on with what you're good at.”

Sugar went on to build a hugely successful business career, founding electronics company Amstrad before later becoming known to millions through The Apprentice.

‌



View 21 Images Alan Sugar (Image: NurPhoto via Getty Images)

Stephen Fry

Stephen Fry struggled at school and was expelled from more than one institution during his teenage years. He eventually returned to education and dramatically turned things around, later winning a place at Cambridge University.

Fry went on to build a long career as an actor, comedian, broadcaster and writer.

‌



View 21 Images Stephen Fry (Image: PA)

Lily Allen

Lily Allen left school at 15 without gaining any GCSEs. Speaking on her BBC podcast Miss Me?, Allen admitted she still felt self-conscious about her education, saying: “I left school when I was 15 and I don't even have one GCSE, not one qualification.”

View 21 Images Lily Allen (Image: Dave Benett/Getty Images)

‌



Joss Stone

Joss Stone left school at 16 with just three GCSEs after struggling academically with dyslexia. She had already begun pursuing music as a teenager and went on to become an internationally successful singer.

View 21 Images Joss Stone (Image: PA)

Lenny Henry

Sir Lenny Henry left school with no qualifications before beginning his career in entertainment as a teenager. He later returned to education, taking English and maths O-levels before eventually earning an English degree from the Open University.

Article continues below

He went on to build a hugely successful career in comedy, acting and television.

View 21 Images Sir Lenny Henry (Image: Stephen Keable/Shutterstock)

For anyone disappointed with their GCSE results, these famous faces prove one set of grades does not necessarily decide what happens next.

News.title: 'Window could have been made safer' before boy, 5, plunged 15 storeys to death
News.content:
'Window could have been made safer' before boy, 5, plunged 15 storeys to death

Aalim Ahmed, five, died instantly after he fell from a 15th-floor kitchen window at a residential block in Plaistow, east London, on May 16 2024

View 3 Images Flowers left at the scene at Jacobs House in Plaistow, London, where five-year-old Aalim Ahmed died (Image: Getty Images)

More could have been done to make a 15th-floor window safer before a five-year-old boy plunged to his death in east London, an inquest heard.

‌



Aalim Ahmed died instantly after he fell from a kitchen window at a residential block in Plaistow shortly before 6am on May 16 2024.

‌



East London Coroner’s Court heard today that Newham Council property manager Nnenna Muoma thought “more restricted features could have been installed” after visiting the Ahmed family that afternoon.

‌



The boy's parents, Makail Ahmed Sahra Osman, previously described their son’s death as “preventable” and blamed Newham Council, after claims Ms Osman reported safety concerns about the flat on multiple occasions.

A post-mortem examination found Aalim died from “multiple injuries due to or as a consequence of trauma” from a “fall from height”.

In a note to the council after seeing the family, property manager Ms Muoma wrote: “Following the horrible incident and fatality, I visited the family yesterday.

‌



View 3 Images Aalim Ahmed fell from a 15th floor flat in east London (Image: PA)

“The kitchen window from where the child fell off is functional but can be operated by a child, hence the incident.

“There is (a) restricted feature to allow a limited opening... More restricted features could have been installed to reduce this risk.”

‌



She told the court: “That was my personal thought. I have seen other households with children with special needs with different gadgets which can be done to make it safer.”

Ms Muoma told the inquest she is not an expert in the area and she did not know the window restrictors in place could be locked. A restrictor is a safety device which is meant to allow the window to only open 50mm-100mm.

Ms Osman previously told the court she was “scared” and “horrified” when Newham Council put them in the top-floor flat, saying Aalim was autistic with “no sense of danger”. She felt the property was not suitable for her young family, which also included a newborn girl, but felt obliged to take it or risk homelessness.

‌



Mourners including other relatives were at the flat when Ms Muoma arrived in the afternoon, asking to speak to Aalim’s mother to offer the family support.

Assistant coroner Ian Wade said: “There was a great deal of tension and emotion and a fraught atmosphere and a number of people were remarking about the council.”

Ms Muoma, who was making the visit on behalf of a colleague who was in charge of the Ahmed case, said she did not respond to any of the remarks.

‌



View 3 Images The boy's parents, Makail Ahmed Sahra Osman, previously described their son’s death as 'preventable' (Image: PA)

A grief-stricken Ms Osman was sitting on a bed with her arms wrapped around herself when Ms Muoma saw her. One of the first things the mother told her was “I asked to be moved and nobody listened to me”.

Ms Muoma told the court: “I said I do not have that information but I am sorry. We want to assist you and if cannot stay overnight I can find you a place to stay.”

‌



A cousin was able to give the family somewhere to stay, the court heard.

After trying to reassure Ms Osman that help would be made available, Ms Muoma asked to see the kitchen because a relative who was in the flat had said this was where the incident happened. She said the female cousin had told her it happened from the right-hand window.

Ms Muoma tried the window twice and was able to open it on the second attempt, but could not remember exactly how she did it.

‌



She said she may have pressed a button to help open it but did not give details about the restrictor or the position of the handle. She also took a photograph of the open position to show her manager how far it can open, she told the court.

Ms Muoma, who was in the flat for less than 20 minutes, said: “It was quite tense. The ladies made a comment saying the council would not move her.”

Yearly inspections by property managers could be made but more could take place if requested, the court heard.

‌



There was a long history of complaints about the flat from the family and Ms Muoma said she did not know if her colleague, who was dealing with the family, was aware of it.

All the windows were closed before the family went to bed, Ms Osman previously told inquest.

Aalim could have been climbing to get a biscuit from a cupboard but the windows had “faulty” restrictors and her ongoing complaints to get them fixed led only to a series of workmen who did not sort the problem, she said.

Article continues below

Biscuits were found on the kitchen table but it is still not known how the child would have got to the window, the court heard.

Ms Osman has previously denied any suggestion she may have “forced” the window open to cope in hot weather.

The hearing continues.

News.title: Wandsworth 'plotting 160% council tax hike' in what is set to be biggest ever bill increase
News.content:
Wandsworth 'plotting 160% council tax hike' in what is set to be biggest ever bill increase

Wandsworth Council, which was a Conservative stronghold for decades, has already been granted permission to raise bills by more than the standard cap after the Government announced a cut in its funding

View Image Council tax bills are normally only allowed to go up by 5% (Image: Getty)

Wandsworth Council is said to be considering a council tax hike of up to 160% - in what would be the biggest increase ever in England.

‌



The council has already been granted permission to raise bills by more than the standard cap after the Government announced a cut in its funding, as part of wider plans to redistribute cashflow toward more deprived regions.

‌



Wandsworth, which is run by a minority Conservative administration after Labour lost control in May, is projected to receive £84million less a year from Whitehall by the end of the decade - a 40% reduction in funding.

‌



But news of a bumper council tax increase comes as households continue to struggle with the cost of living, with inflation confirmed to have risen to 2.9% last month.

Wandsworth, which is in southwest London, currently has the lowest Band D council tax bills at approximately £1,028 per year - in comparison, the average Band D council tax bill across England is £2,392.

We also treat our community members to special offers, promotions, and adverts from us and our partners. If you don’t like our community, you can check out any time you like. If you’re curious, you can read our Privacy Notice. NEWSLETTER: Or sign up to the Mirror's Money newsletter here for all the best advice and shopping deals straight to your inbox.

‌



If approved, council tax in Wandsworth would be hiked from April 2027 and then frozen for the rest of the term, according to Parliament website PoliticsHome.

The maximum amount most councils in England can normally raise bills without a referendum is 5%. Wandsworth Labour leader Simon Hogg said: “When Labour ran Wandsworth Council we had the lowest council tax in the country, the highest reserves of any neighbouring borough and no external debt.

“The new Conservative administration has brought chaos. They are extreme and divided and clearly don’t have a plan for how to run the council. “The Conservatives are pretending the council has run out of money so they can bring in austerity policies. They’ve already cut domestic abuse services, scrapped the youth bus and axed new council homes for 400 local people. “They now intend to massively increase council tax. It beggars belief that Wandsworth Conservatives are planning Britain’s biggest ever council tax increase.”

‌



It is understood that a final decision has not yet been made. Wandsworth Council declined to comment.

A spokesperson from the Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government said: “Decisions on whether to increase council tax are ultimately for local authorities to make and justify but we continue to expect any decisions to put taxpayers first.

“The flexibility given to Wandsworth Council is time limited and we’re making £278million available for them by 2028-29.”

‌



The biggest council tax increases before this were by North Somerset, Shropshire and Worcestershire, who were all given special permission to enforce a 9% rise this April.

Westminster, Kensington and Chelsea, Hammersmith and Fulham, and City of London, alongside Windsor and Maidenhead, have also been granted permission to increase council tax by more than 5% from next April.

The Telegraph reported earlier this month that Westminster council is considering raising council tax by 100%.

‌



Cut your council tax bill

Check if you are entitled to a council tax discount. For example, if you live alone, you get 25% off your council tax bill. The maximum 100% discount is awarded if someone lives alone is considered to be "severely mentally impairment" and is claiming benefits, or if you live in an all-student household.

There are also Council Tax Support or Council Tax Reduction schemes for people claiming benefits or on low incomes. The exact help varies between councils but your bill could be reduced by up to 100%.

Not everyone is in the right council tax band - and if you're accidentally in too high of a band, you could be owed thousands of pounds back, plus lower bills going forward.

Article continues below

But do your research, as if you're in too low of a band, you could get moved up and your bills will become more expensive. Your neighbours could also end up being bumped up.

News.title: 'My sexless marriage is a prison sentence - husband refuses to answer one question'
News.content:
'My sexless marriage is a prison sentence - husband refuses to answer one question'

Agony aunt Coleen Nolan advises a reader who knows there are issues with her marriage but is starting to resent her husband for not addressing them and ignoring the problems

View Image She said she wants to address their issues but her husband won't (Image: Shared Content Unit)

Dear Coleen

My husband and I are both 40, we don't have children – it just never happened for us – and have been together for 10 years. I'm sick of pretending our relationship is OK and can't face another decade of the same old thing.

‌



We're a good team, we like the same things and get on well, but there's no affection and sex is a rare occurrence. We're like friends with (occasional) benefits. He's always been very selfish and cut off, and whenever I try to be affectionate, he tenses up or pushes me away. The constant rejection is soul-destroying and being together seems pointless.

‌



It seems that he'd rather ignore the elephant in the room and carry on, like our marriage is some kind of prison sentence to be endured. He's so bad at communicating and being honest about how he feels. If I do try to talk about our relationship, he gets irritated and sulks, which can go on for days, and until things slowly get back to 'normal'.

‌



I find the way he reacts to things so childish and I'm really starting to resent him. What's going to change things and how can I get through to him?

Coleen says

You mention children not happening for you and I wonder if this was a long-held dream that you had to give up on. And maybe the end of that dream has left you a bit directionless and wondering how you move forward as a couple. It's something to consider and maybe you haven't really faced this disappointment together and talked about what your future looks like without kids. Maybe that's another elephant in the room.

‌



I do understand how difficult it is when a partner won't open up and have the conversations that could help you to figure out what to do. It might sound crazy when you live with someone, but writing a letter to them can be a good way of breaking down the barrier, it's something I've done in the past.

Start by saying that you want to talk, and you know he finds it hard, but you can't keep ignoring the problems in your marriage and, if you can't discuss it and come up with ways to make things better, then you can't carry on. Be really honest about how you feel. I certainly felt better for writing everything down.

The bottom line is, you can't fix something on your own. You could suggest counselling, but unless he's willing to engage, you have a tough choice to make. Good luck.

Article continues below

Coleen's words of wisdom

Cherish that person who makes you feel lighter and good about yourself when you talk to them. The type of person who accepts you for who you are and offers kindness and support instead of judgement. Invest in that friendship.

News.title: 'Millions of extra brews being drunk by nervous parents' as kids await GCSE results
News.content:
'Millions of extra brews being drunk by nervous parents' as kids await GCSE results

A survey by Yorkshire Tea has found kettles will be boiling more frequently than normal as all-important exam results are awaited and nerves are set jangling

View Image Tea could provide comfort as exam nerves kick in (Image: Anton Moskovchenko via Getty Images)

Millions of extra brews are expected to be drunk by nervous parents awaiting their kids' GCSE results, a study suggests.

‌



Research by Yorkshire Tea claims two in five (40%) parents will reach for multiple brews as results land, with one in 10 knocking back at least four extra cups to steady their nerves. With hundreds of thousands of students set to receive their results, the Yorkshire-based tea experts believe more cups of tea could be drunk than any other day of the year.

‌



Kettles could be working overtime, with more than a third (38%) of parents saying a proper cup of tea is the best way to keep a lid on their Results Day jitters. Research also revealed almost half of parents (44%) believe 'Shall we put the kettle on?' is a better way to break the ice while discussing what their children's results were.

‌



Couple marking unique double celebration get TWO cards from the King and Queen READ MORE :

UK heatwaves give way to rain for some as Brits welcome relief from scorching temperatures READ MORE :

Further findings suggest hundreds of thousands of families will celebrate with a cup of tea too, with 39% of parents saying they’d rather toast their child’s results with a proper brew than an alcoholic drink.

Penny Webster, brand manager at Yorkshire Tea, said: “The stress and anticipation of results day is enough to bring the whole family to boiling point so it’s no surprise that kettles will be working overtime this week.

“Before asking about grades, offering to put the kettle on and making a proper brew can give everyone a moment to gather themselves before properly digesting the results, whether they've gone the way you hoped, or not. And whatever is written on that results sheet, we'll be sure to be there to support the nation's families on GCSE results day."

‌



With millions of extra cups to be drunk, Yorkshire Tea has reminded parents how to make a proper cup of tea by following five simple but important steps.

Step 1: Treat your water kindly

Penny said: "Run the tap a little so the water’s nicely aerated and only boil it once to keep the oxygen level up. Oxygen in water helps flavour!"

‌



Step 2: Add tea and water

Penny said: "Pop a tea bag into your mug, pour over the hot water and stir briefly."

Step 3: Wait patiently

Penny said: "Tea needs time to unlock all its flavour, so give it 4-5 minutes to do its thing. This is a perfect time to munch a sneaky biscuit or daydream about holidays."

Article continues below

Step 4: Give it a squeeze

Penny said: "Before removing the tea bag, gently squidge it against the side of the mug. Just the once, mind – if you really mash it, it'll taste bitter."

Step 5: Customise your brew

Penny said: "We like a splash of semi-skimmed or whole milk, but your brew is unique to you – so add milk, sugar, honey, lemon or nothing at all. Most importantly, enjoy!"

News.title: Few days left to get free fruit at Tesco UK stores as offer ends soon
News.content:
Few days left to get free fruit at Tesco UK stores as offer ends soon

Certain shoppers only have a handful of days left until the offer ends

View 2 Images The offer is running until August 30 (Image: Getty )

Tesco shoppers only have a few days left to take advantage of the store's 'free fruit' scheme. Certain customers will be able to get their hands on free apples at the checkout until August 30, which is eleven days away, at the time of writing.

‌



The popular supermarket brought back its free fruit for kids program as the summer holidays started back in July. While many families enjoy the break, it can also put a strain on household budgets. To help out while schools are still closed, Tesco is giving away free apples. Children can pick up a piece of fruit at checkouts in more than 800 large stores and 77 Express locations.

‌



Eating whole, unpeeled apples offers significant health benefits, including a high water content (around 85%), soluble and insoluble fibre, and protective antioxidants such as quercetin. A medium-sized apple contains about 95 calories and helps keep you hydrated and feeling full.

‌



Tesco hopes this gives millions of children a healthy snack during the weekly shop. The offer runs throughout the peak of the holidays, running from July 20 until August 30. Parents using Click and Collect at participating stores can also get free apples for their kids when picking up groceries.

Announcing the news on Instagram in July, Tesco wrote: "Free Fruit for Kids is back this summer to help children get one of their five a day. From 20 July to 30 August, children can pick up a free apple at over 800 large Tesco stores and selected Express stores. Click and Collect customers will also be given free apples for their children at selected stores. Subject to availability."

Content cannot be displayed without consent

‌



The free fruit scheme was first launched in 2016 as a healthier alternative to checkout sweets and chocolates. Looking ahead, Tesco aims to give one million students free fruit and vegetables by July 2029. It also runs a Free Fruit and Veg for Schools scheme with the British Nutrition Foundation.

Tesco says: "We want to help one million school kids get fruit and veg for free. Because every little helps. Our Free Fruit and Veg for Schools programme is providing access to fruit and veg across over 500 schools in the UK, supporting thousands of children get more of their five-a-day."

In addition to the free fruit, Tesco brought back its "Kids Eat Free" deal in its store cafés for families eating out. Available across 317 cafés during the holidays, the scheme now includes weekends. Adults buying any item from 60p can get a free kids' hot meal, breakfast, or Pick 'n' Mix deal by showing their Clubcard.

‌



View 2 Images Besides the free apples for kids, Tesco is also running its "Kids Eat Free" deal

Shoppers can also buy pre-filled donation bags in stores to help local food banks. The Trussell Trust reports that food bank support for children remains 34% higher than before the pandemic.

The donation bags cost between £2 and £4 and contain healthy, non-perishable food. Donated items go directly to Felix and Trussell to support families in need across the UK.

Article continues below

Claire De Silva from Tesco said: "We want to be able to support our charity partners to help those needing a little extra support this summer. Our partnerships with Felix and Trussell are central to this aim. When you’re out doing your weekly shop this summer, dropping a few tins into a food collection point, picking up a food donation bag in our stores or rounding up our grocery bill, can make a difference to the lives of thousands of children in communities across the UK."

News.title: UK heatwaves give way to rain for some as Brits welcome relief from scorching temperatures
News.content:
UK heatwaves give way to rain for some as Brits welcome relief from scorching temperatures

Weather relief came for many Brits as rainfall finally reached some areas after weeks of droughts and extreme heat across the nation.

This summer, the UK faced severe weather as half of England and all of Wales were declared to officially be in drought and hosepipe bans were announced by 10 water companies.

Rainfall has been unusually dry with Kew Gardens, in London, recording its first completely dry calendar month since record began in 1871, as not a drop of rain was recorded in July. Signs that this weather misery could soon be over for the year were spotted today after parts of the UK were hit by "heavy pulses" of rain early on Wednesday.

Several residents in Hampshire even posed with their arms wide open welcoming the dark rain clouds above them. Some areas in the country were predicted to have the "first meaningful rain for a long time" this week, the Met Office said.

The forecaster also issued yellow warnings for thunderstorms in northern areas of England and Wales from Wednesday evening through to Thursday morning. Alerts were also issued for Northern Ireland from midday to midnight on Wednesday and for an area of eastern Scotland around Aberdeen from 2pm-9pm on Wednesday. Despite the news of rain, the UK is also facing the risk of surface water floods as heavy rain falls on baked dry ground, which is unable to absorb water effectively.

News.title: Track defect found on approach to site of Lewes derailment, initial report says
News.content:
A defect was found on railway tracks in East Sussex at the site where a train derailed leaving 30 injured, a report says.

Initial findings from the Rail Accident Investigation Branch (RAIB) found an "irregularity" with the tracks near Lewes where three carriages tumbled down an embankment last Thursday.

The RAIB, which is continuing to investigate the derailment, said it had received "several reports of rough riding at the location of the derailment from passengers on other trains".

Network Rail and Greater Thameslink Railway, whose Southern Rail train was involved in the crash, said in a joint statement they were "sorry this happened on our railway".

Investigators from the RAIB have said CCTV from a train which passed through the crash site at 14:04 BST showed the "irregularity" with the track geometry just before the point where the train came off the tracks.

The 14:24 service from London Victoria to Eastbourne derailed in the Landport area of Lewes at about 15:54 BST.

The derailment left two people seriously injured, and 18 were taken to hospital with less serious injuries. The 18 have since left hospital.

News.title: Thunderstorm warnings issued for parts of UK with flash flooding expected
News.content:
Yellow thunderstorm warnings have been issued across the UK, with heavy showers expected to lead to flash flooding and travel disruption.

The Met Office warnings will come into force across northern England, Northern Ireland and eastern Scotland later in the day on Wednesday. The warning for northern England will remain in place until Thursday morning.

The downpours follow almost two months of dry weather, with parts of the country experiencing their first rain in weeks on Tuesday.

People in areas impacted by thunderstorms have been told by the Met Office to expect that businesses and homes could flood, transport services could be delayed and power cuts are likely.

The yellow weather warnings are in place for:

Northern Ireland from 12:00 until 23:59 BST on Wednesday

Parts of North East Scotland, including Aberdeen, from 14:00 until 21:00 on Wednesday

Parts of the North of England, including Manchester and Newcastle upon Tyne, from 19:00 until 10:00 on Thursday

The Met Office said lightning, hail and thunder were expected in the areas affected by warnings, with up to 30mm of rain expected within a few hours in parts of North East Scotland and across Northern Ireland.

Parts of northern England could see up to 50mm of rain within six hours.

Much of the UK has seen a mixture of sunshine and scattered showers already on Wednesday.

In Wisley, Surrey, a 62-day long dry spell was broken on Wednesday morning, with the remarkable run ending after 1.6mm fell before 10.00.

News.title: Salmonella outbreak: What we know so far
News.content:
The UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) has recently declared a national outbreak, external of salmonella food poisoning after one person died and hundreds more fell ill with the bug.

Although not yet proven, imported eggs or products containing them are the leading suspects as to the cause.

Evidence also suggests people caught the bug while eating out, rather than at home - with catering and food services such as restaurants or cafes likely to play a part.

But there is still a lot to be discovered.

What do we know and what questions remain?

News.title: Israel opens up tenders for controversial West Bank settlement project
News.content:
Israel has built about 160 settlements housing 700,000 Jews since it occupied the West Bank and East Jerusalem - land Palestinians want, along with Gaza, for a hoped-for future state - during the 1967 Middle East war. An estimated 3.3 million Palestinians live alongside them.

Despite the fierce international opposition, successive Israeli governments have allowed settlements to grow.

However, expansion has risen sharply since Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu returned to power in late 2022 at the head of a right-wing, pro-settler coalition, as well as the start of the Gaza war, triggered by Hamas's 7 October 2023 attack on Israel.

Under international pressure, Israel held off for decades on plans to build in E1.

Many of its allies and Palestinians argued these would deal a major blow to hopes of a two-state solution, effectively bisecting the West Bank.

But the current Israeli government gave the go-ahead for E1 construction a year ago, expressly to "erase" the idea of a Palestinian state.

Despite an Israeli court challenge to the plans by Bedouin Palestinians living in the area and Israeli peace groups, the housing ministry has now issued a tender for 1,234 of the 3,401 housing units approved by the Israeli government last August.

It covers about 12 sq km (4.6 sq miles) between East Jerusalem and the settlement of Maale Adumim

At the time of their unveiling, Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich, who is ultranationalist and settler, said the idea of a Palestinian state was "being erased".

The deadline for bids is 19 October, just days before Israel's general election on 27 October. That should enable the government to sign deals with contractors that it would be much harder for a future government to cancel.

News.title: 'Incredible': SpaceX rocket spotted off Christmas Island coast
News.content:
A SpaceX rocket has made an unexpected appearance off Christmas Island after touching down in the Indian Ocean following a test flight from Texas on 24 July.

David Watchorn, chair of the Christmas Island Tourism Association said he initially thought he was looking at ships on his way to work, before realising it was "a rocket, a space rocket" being towed.

The 52-metre long rocket has caused a stir among locals, with some "sneaking out" of work for a glimpse, and others preparing their boats for a closer look at the debris.

"It's really incredible to think about what it's been through," Watchorn told the BBC.

"The more and more you look at it, the more fascinating it's becoming".

News.title: BBC presenter Emma Barnett reveals she 'had the hysterectomy I never wanted to have'
News.content:
BBC presenter Emma Barnett has revealed she had a hysterectomy and surgery for endometriosis days before a documentary she made about the condition was broadcast.

Barnett, 41, returned to Radio 4's Today programme on Wednesday morning, explaining she had been absent in recent weeks because she was in hospital "in a case of life imitating work".

She told listeners: "I made a programme on endometriosis on BBC Two and ended up being in hospital for endometriosis.

"So yes, I've been recuperating, shall we say, from surgery for endometriosis and a hysterectomy to boot. So that's been less fun than the Today programme, but it is lovely to be back."

Barnett's announcement came soon after she published a blog about the "hysterectomy I never wanted to have", external.

The presenter, who has two children, said it was "totally surreal" to be in hospital on the night her documentary was broadcast in June, only well enough to watch the final 10 minutes.

"Some 48 hours before the documentary aired - I had undergone a near-5 hour surgery and somehow found myself lying in bed recovering from extensive endometriosis surgery, a hysterectomy and a gallbladder removal," she wrote.

"Triple threat. Go big or go home. Life imitating art."

She added: "I felt blind-sided and robbed, even though my care had been superb and doctors, utterly brilliant.

"But this was not the road I had envisioned for myself. I had the hysterectomy I never wanted to have."

Endometriosis is where cells similar to those in the lining of the womb grow in other parts of the body, resulting in what Barnett has described as "bone-grinding, life-altering pain". It affects one in 10 women and there is no known cure.

A hysterectomy is a surgical procedure to remove the womb (uterus). A hysterectomy alongside removal of endometriosis can reduce the risk of recurrence, according to Endometriosis UK, external.

In her blog, Barnett also said she suspected most of her pain may have been down to another condition, adenomyosis, which can be treated by a hysterectomy.

Her surgery was necessitated after she had an ultrasound while filming the final scene of the documentary, and a problem in her gallbladder was found. "Suddenly things became urgent and non negotiable."

The broadcaster added that she was hopeful that the surgery had helped.

She wrote: "Early indications are that the pain is very much improved - although I am still healing from the surgery itself so that also feels uncertain and frightening to admit - even to myself."

News.title: Jump in energy bills drives UK inflation to highest rate for four months
News.content:
Higher energy bills drove UK inflation up to 2.9% in the year to July, the highest level in four months, according to new figures.

Gas prices soared at the sharpest pace in almost four years, the Office for National Statistics (ONS) said, leading to an increase in the cap on household energy bills in July. Energy costs surged after US-Israel war with Iran began, which has restricted global oil supplies.

July's reading is the highest since March but some price growth slowed. Food inflation, at 1.3%, is at its lowest rate for close to five years.

Experts said the inflation figure is unlikely to influence the Bank of England to change its key interest rate at its next meeting in September.

Energy costs for households rose on 1 July after Ofgem, the energy regulator, increased the price cap on gas and electricity costs by 13%, which added Â£221 a year to the typical bill.

Homes are forecast to see a 4% rise in energy bills from October, according to Cornwall Insight, which would take them to the highest level since July 2023.

There is ongoing uncertainty over the US-Iran conflict, which has seen effective closures of the Strait of Hormuz, a key trading passage for ships carrying oil, liquefied natural gas and other commodities.

Cornwall Insight, an independent energy consultancy, added that energy price pressures were being compounded by the ongoing heatwave across Europe "increasing gas demand for power generation to meeting air conditioning and cooling demand".

News.title: PM unveils plan to get rough sleepers off streets for Christmas
News.content:
Every rough sleeper in England will be offered accommodation this winter, the prime minister has said.

Andy Burnham made ending rough sleeping his first pledge when entering Downing Street in July and now says he wants "to get everyone in for Christmas".

Emergency accommodation will be provided to end the need for rough sleeping alongside practical support for any health needs, as part of a Â£442m package.

Conservative shadow housing secretary Sir James Cleverly said Burnham promised to end rough sleeping in Greater Manchester when mayor of the area but "failed because he didn't do the hard work necessary".

Burnham's pledge seeks to build on the success of Everyone In, a Covid pandemic-era scheme that saw thousands of rough sleepers housed in hotels and temporary accommodation.

About 37,000 people were helped by that scheme, following its launch in March 2020. The charity Shelter found that about a quarter of them had found settled accommodation, in the form of housing lasting at least six months., external

The PM's announcement comes with an additional Â£102m in new funding, taking Burnham's total commitment to tackling rough sleeping to Â£442m since becoming prime minister.

The money is said to be "fully funded" within the Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government.

As well as providing immediate support to get people off the streets, the funding is also designed to deliver more than 1,000 homes over the next three years to provide rough sleepers with permanent accommodation.

The funding will also provide "intensive wraparound support", typically psychiatric and drug and alcohol services to help people rebuild their lives.

Burnham said he did not believe "anybody should be forced to sleep rough".

He added: "And actually when you do leave people sleeping rough it can often cost more to the state because people can be in and out of A&E, in and out of hospital beds and sometimes in contact with the police."

The prime minister said the government funding "may not fully get us there" as he appealed to charities and faith organisations to help ensure an offer is made to everybody who needs it.

He added: "We did it in the pandemic. We can do it again."

Rooms in shared flats or houses, B&B accommodation, warm spaces for short-term refuge and supported lodgings are among the types of accommodation mentioned in the government's guidance that could be used to bring people in off the streets.

Burnham also told The Big Issue, external he would commit to donating 15% of his prime minister's salary to tackle homelessness, which follows his decision to give 15% of his MP salary to causes in his Makerfield constituency.

A prime minister is entitled to an additional salary of Â£83,837 on top of their salary for being an MP. Recent PMs have claimed Â£75,440, with the previous government of Sir Keir Starmer continuing the freeze on ministerial salaries.

News.title: Jury discharged in Palestine Action Elbit raid trial
News.content:
A jury has been discharged in the trial of eight Palestine Action activists who were accused of helping to organise a raid on the UK site of an Israel-based defence firm.

Ian Sanders, Aleksandra Herbich, Teuta Hoxha, Sean Middleborough, Julija Brigadirova, Hannah Davidson, Madeleine Norman and William Plastow were charged with criminal damage after a raid on Elbit Systems in Filton, near Bristol, in August 2024.

They were all also charged with violent disorder, although Plastow was previously found not guilty of this offence.

The group denied any wrongdoing and have been on trial at the Old Bailey since 22 June. Judge Patrick Field discharged the jury earlier after 37 hours of deliberations.

The court heard none of the defendants were at Elbit during raid but were alleged to have helped to plan it, including by compiling an equipment list, reconnaissance, purchasing tools and weapons used by others, and co-ordinating the break-in and its filming.

The Crown Prosecution Service will now need to decide whether to seek a retrial.

A hearing has been set for 14 September to decide the future of the case.
